findings.F1: Step 5's main measure is on the side the idea predicts but short of the bar: the slope of the 5-day excess return on the forecast is +0.00057 with t 1.08, over 819 grid cases on 374 days. The size agrees: the unusual move is +0.43 % per case in the short direction, with t 1.35 over 734 days and a strength of 0.051. That is about what real ideas show, but this sample cannot tell it from 0.
findings.F2: In the visible folds B and C the same regression is clearer on the 5-day horizon. On the forecast it gives t 2.46 (287 cases); on the raw depth it gives t 2.96, a slope of 0.0095 per unit of depth. The deepest third shows an excess return of -3.31 % against -0.33 % for the shallowest third. Since all four folds give only t 1.08, folds A and D must carry a weaker or noisier version of the same sign, so the gap is one of precision, not of direction.
findings.F3: The effect is mostly in the deepest closes, as a graded idea predicts it should be strongest there. The deepest fifth (mean depth -6.2 daily swings) is followed by -5.5 % excess over 5 days. The next four fifths (depth -3.9 to -0.9) sit between -0.6 % and +0.4 %. A few tail cases therefore carry the slope, which is what makes it noisy at this sample size.
findings.F4: The sign holds across the horizons in folds B and C: depth slope t 1.42 at 1 day (1484 cases), 1.28 at 3 days (494), 2.96 at 5 days (287) and 2.37 at 10 days (143). The plan's 5-day horizon is where it shows best, so the test was not measured in the wrong place.
findings.F5: The effect varies by period but is not confined to one part of the data, so no condition isolates it.
findings.F6: The market's own drift drowns the effect in the book. The coins' normal drift is -0.57 % per case in the short direction, so the total move is -0.14 % against a cost of 0.19 % per trade. The unusual move is 2.2 times the cost, but too uncertain to rely on with six coins.

ideas.name: choppy deep close, more coins
ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the further a coin's close sits below its 20-day high, measured in units of the standard deviation of its daily returns over the last 20 days, the larger its fall over the next five days.
ideas.consequence: A deep close below a sideways range's top is a reason to hold a short for about a week rather than a day, since the breakdown unfolds over several sessions and moves enough to cover the cost of the trade.
